headline: US electronics factory-gate prices rise fastest on record for the sector
text:
# US electronics factory-gate prices rise fastest on record for the sector

Chip-era price pressure in US electronics is the freshest number on the page; Europe's energy data show bills rising again even as coal generation and diesel cars disappear.

## Today in the data

### Electronics prices up 12.9%

[US electronics factory-gate prices and chip output, yoy](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)

US PPI for computer and electronic products was 120.0 in Aug 2026, up 12.9% on a year earlier (us-ppi-sectors); the usual yearly change is +0.6%. Look at how flat the blue line is before 2025 — this sector normally has falling prices. Worth checking against semiconductor output, up 11.9% in Jul 2026 (us-chips), though the Fed's quality adjustment inflates that index.

### Austrian bills jump a third

[Household electricity price, EUR per kWh, all taxes](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)

Austrian households paid €0.3272 per kWh in H2 2025, up 34.3% on H2 2024 and the largest rise since 2008 (energy-household-eu). Luxembourg rose 31.7% to €0.2665; Germany is still dearer at €0.3869. The base matters: H2 2024 was Austria's cheapest half-year since 2021, so relief measures ending are worth checking against.

### UK coal power effectively gone

[UK electricity generation by source, TWh](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)

UK coal generated 0.33 TWh in 2025, down 82.6% from 1.9 TWh in 2024, the sharpest fall in a record from 1921 (electricity-mix). On the chart, wind at 85.8 TWh has almost caught gas at 90.9 TWh. The last year is often Ember's provisional figure, and this is generation, not consumption.

### Egypt's FDI falls back 31bn

[Egypt: net FDI inflows, current US dollars, 1971-2025](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)

Egypt's net FDI inflow was $15.45bn in 2025, down $31.1bn from $46.6bn in 2024, the sharpest fall since 1971 (macro-external, World Bank WDI). The chart shows 2024 as a single spike far above everything before it, so this is a return to trend rather than a collapse. WDI figures for the latest year are revised often.

### Austrian pharma output halves

[Austrian industrial production: pharma vs manufacturing, 2021=100](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)

Austrian pharma production (C21) was 160.4 in Jul 2026, down 45.7% on Jul 2025, the sharpest fall since the series starts in 2011 (eu-ipi-sectors). Total manufacturing sat at 102.6, barely moving, so this is one sector, not the economy. Pharma batch production swings violently month to month; the July figure is early and revision-prone.

### Estonia's new-car market halves

[New passenger car registrations in Estonia, 2014-2025](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)

Estonia registered 13,141 new cars in 2025, down 49% from 25,744 in 2024; diesels fell 70.4% to 1,738 (eu-car-registrations). The two lines fall together, so this is a market-wide drop with diesel worst hit — a car-registration tax introduced in 2025 is worth checking against. A twelve-year record makes "record fall" a modest claim.

### Greek renewables pass 60%

[Greece: renewables as a share of electricity, 2005-2025](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)

Greece's renewable share of electricity reached 60.9% in 2025, up 9.65 points on 2024, the biggest annual gain since 2005 (eu-renewables-share). The chart's climb is steady from 2010 onwards; this year's step is roughly four times the usual 2.17 points. The figure follows the Renewable Energy Directive's accounting rules, so it differs from Ember's generation share.

## Forecasts

### US electronics prices keep climbing

[us-ppi-sectors:computer_electronic forecast, 3 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)

The last observation is 120.048 in Aug 2026 (us-ppi-sectors). The tool chose Holt-Winters additive with period 12 and fits the past closely, a mean absolute error of 0.22% in sample. It projects 122.8 by Nov 2026, with a 95% band of 121.4 to 124.3. The band is only the spread of past residuals widened with horizon, so it assumes the present trend continues. A tariff change, a memory-price turn or a downward BLS revision to the summer months would put the outcome outside it.

### Austrian bills level off next year

[energy-household-eu:AT forecast, 2 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)

The last observation is €0.3272 per kWh in H2 2025 (energy-household-eu). Holt-Winters additive, period 2, fits with a 3.3% mean absolute error and projects €0.3249 in H2 2026, band €0.2904 to €0.3594 — no further rise, but no reversal either. The band reflects how much past half-years have deviated from this kind of trend. This is a taxed, partly administered price: the projection extrapolates its history, not any announced policy. A new levy, a tariff freeze or a wholesale-price shock would break it.

### Austrian pharma output: wide and uncertain

[eu-ipi-sectors:AT|C21 forecast, 3 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)

The last observation is 160.4 in Jul 2026 (eu-ipi-sectors). Holt-Winters additive, period 12, fits with a 5.0% mean absolute error and projects 165.7 in Oct 2026, band 119.1 to 212.4 — a range so wide it barely constrains anything, which is the honest reading of a series that jumped from 295 to 160 in a year. The band is past residual spread, and here those residuals are huge. Any single large production campaign, or a Eurostat revision to July, moves the level outside it.

## Correlations

- **Austria vs Luxembourg household electricity** (yoy, 2008-S2 to 2025-S2, n=35): r = 0.53 at lag 0 and 0.61 with Luxembourg leading by one half-year, both clearing the 0.36 band. Central-European retail tariffs move together, which makes the current Austrian jump look regional rather than local.
- **US semiconductor output vs electronics PPI** (yoy, 2012-01 to 2026-07, n=175): r = 0.01 at lag 0, strongest |r| = 0.14 at lag −12, not distinguishable from zero against a 0.42 band. Volume and price in this sector carry no usable lead-lag relation, so the chip-output story is a hypothesis only.

## What to watch

- **cpi-eu and eu-hicp** (last 2026-07): the August prints settle whether European energy bills are still feeding headline inflation.
- **eu-ipi-sectors** (last 2026-07): the August figure says whether Austrian pharma's −45.7% was a one-month batch effect.
- **us-ppi-sectors** (last 2026-08): the September print, due next month, tests whether 12.9% is a peak.
- **eu-ppi-sectors** (last 2026-08): European factory-gate prices next to the US electronics move.
- **eu-vet-weight**: no 2026 weights exist yet — Eurostat's ECOICOP2 rebase means Belgium's 3.63 per mille cannot be extended until a successor dataset appears.

## Sources

- us-ppi-sectors — BLS producer price indexes by NAICS industry via FRED, not seasonally adjusted, monthly; last 2026-08.
- us-chips — Federal Reserve industrial production via FRED (NAICS 3344, 334), monthly, seasonally adjusted; last 2026-07.
- energy-household-eu — Eurostat nrg_pc_204, band DC, all taxes, EUR/kWh, semi-annual; last 2025-S2.
- electricity-mix — Ember Yearly Electricity Data and Energy Institute Statistical Review via Our World in Data; last 2025.
- macro-external — World Bank World Development Indicators; last 2025.
- eu-ipi-sectors — Eurostat sts_inpr_m, 2021=100, monthly; last 2026-07.
- eu-car-registrations — Eurostat road_eqr_carpda, annual; last 2025.
- eu-renewables-share — Eurostat nrg_ind_ren, annual; last 2025.
- eu-vet-weight — Eurostat HICP item weights, CP0935; last 2025.
